enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,

term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

outstanding borrowings under the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

Item 8.01.
Other Events.

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (PepsiCo) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of
May 27, 2022, among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 364 Day Credit
Agreement). There were no outstanding borrowings under the 2022 364 Day Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,
and expires on May 24, 2024. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the
2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or
Euros. PepsiCo may request renewal of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement for an additional 364 day period or convert any amounts outstanding into a
term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo terminated the $3,800,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of May 27, 2022, among
PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement). There were no
outstanding borrowings under the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 Five Year Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, including a $750,000,000 swing line
subfacility for Euro-denominated borrowings permitted to be borrowed on a same day basis, subject to customary terms and conditions, and expires on
May 26, 2028. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the 2023 Five Year
Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros. PepsiCo
may, once a year, request renewal of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement for an additional one year period. Subject to certain conditions stated in the 2023
Five Year Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under the 2023 Five Year Credit
Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement may be used
for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement contains customary representations and warranties
and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement and their affiliates have
engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo and its affiliates.SUBMIT

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-37#opus47-r1", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "No. Based on FY2022 data, American Water Works had NEGATIVE working capital of approximately -$1,561 million (Total current assets of $1,250M minus Total current liabilities of $2,811M).

However, working capital is not a particularly meaningful metric for American Water Works. As a regulated water utility, the company:
- Generates highly predictable, recurring cash flows from a large, stable ratepayer base, so it does not need a large current-asset cushion.
- Routinely funds operations with short-term debt/commercial paper (note the $1,175M of short-term debt and $281M current portion of long-term debt in FY2022, which together drive most of the negative working capital) that is regularly refinanced into long-term debt.
- Is capital-intensive, with the vast majority of its assets tied up in long-lived property, plant and equipment ($23.2B) rather than current assets.
Negative working capital is therefore normal and structural for utilities like AWK and not a sign of liquidity distress."}

Does Boeing have an improving gross margin profile as of FY2022? If gross margin is not a useful metric for a company like this, then state that and explain why.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-51#opus47-r1", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 1.0, "final_answer": "Yes\u2014technically Boeing's gross margin has been improving. Using total revenue less total costs and expenses (cost of products, cost of services, and Boeing Capital interest expense), gross margin moved from roughly -9.8% in FY2020 to ~4.8% in FY2021 to ~5.3% in FY2022, so the trajectory is positive.\n\nThat said, gross margin is a somewhat limited metric for Boeing. As a long-cycle aerospace/defense manufacturer, Boeing uses program and contract accounting where cost of sales incorporates estimated total program costs, reach-forward losses, abnormal production costs (e.g., 737 MAX grounding, 787 rework), and charges tied to fixed-price defense development contracts. These lumpy, non-recurring charges cause reported cost of goods sold \u2014 and therefore gross margin \u2014 to swing sharply year to year in ways that don't reflect the underlying unit economics. Analysts typically focus instead on segment operating margins (especially Boeing Commercial Airplanes and Boeing Defense, Space & Security), program margins, backlog, free cash flow, and deliveries, which better capture the economics of the business than a consolidated gross margin."}

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (PepsiCo) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of
May 27, 2022, among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 364 Day Credit
Agreement). There were no outstanding borrowings under the 2022 364 Day Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,
and expires on May 24, 2024. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the
2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or
Euros. PepsiCo may request renewal of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement for an additional 364 day period or convert any amounts outstanding into a
term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo terminated the $3,800,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of May 27, 2022, among
PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement). There were no
outstanding borrowings under the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 Five Year Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, including a $750,000,000 swing line
subfacility for Euro-denominated borrowings permitted to be borrowed on a same day basis, subject to customary terms and conditions, and expires on
May 26, 2028. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the 2023 Five Year
Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros. PepsiCo
may, once a year, request renewal of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement for an additional one year period. Subject to certain conditions stated in the 2023
Five Year Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under the 2023 Five Year Credit
Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement may be used
for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement contains customary representations and warranties

parties, we make, market, distribute and sell a wide variety of beverages and convenient foods, serving customers and consumers
in more than 200 countries and territories.

Net sales increased 18.3% to $10.2 billion compared to $8.6 billion in fiscal 2021,
primarily due to the favorable impact from the continued resilience of the beauty
category, retail price increases, the impact of new brands and product innovation,
increased social occasions, and fewer COVID-19 limitations compared to fiscal 2021.
Comparable sales increased 15.6% compared to an increase of 37.9% in fiscal 2021,
driven by a 10.8% increase in transactions and a 4.3% increase in average ticket.
Gross profit increased 20.1% to $4.0 billion compared to $3.4 billion in fiscal 2021. As
a percentage of net sales, gross profit increased to 39.6% compared to 39.0% in fiscal
2021, primarily due to leverage of fixed costs, strong growth in other revenue, and
favorable channel mix shifts, partially offset by higher inventory shrink and lower
merchandise margin.

2021. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased to 23.5% compared to
23.9% in fiscal 2021, primarily due to lower marketing expenses and leverage of
incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits
due to wage investments.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-23#opus47-r2", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "Amcor's quick ratio improved slightly between FY2022 and FY2023.

Using (Cash + Trade Receivables) / Current Liabilities:
- FY2022: ($775 + $1,935) / $5,103 ≈ 0.53
- FY2023: ($689 + $1,875) / $4,476 ≈ 0.57

Even including prepaid/other current assets ((Current Assets − Inventories − Assets held for sale) / Current Liabilities), the ratio rose from ~0.63 in FY2022 to ~0.69 in FY2023. The improvement was driven primarily by a meaningful reduction in current liabilities (mainly trade payables and short-term debt) that outpaced the modest decline in cash and receivables.

Note: The quick ratio remains below 1.0 in both years, which is common for a large, investment-grade packaging manufacturer like Amcor that relies on stable operating cash flow and revolving credit facilities rather than holding a large buffer of liquid assets."}

Does American Water Works have positive working capital based on FY2022 data? If working capital is not a useful or relevant metric for this company, then please state that and explain why.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-37#opus47-r2", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "No. Based on FY2022 data, American Water Works had NEGATIVE working capital of approximately -$1,561 million (Total current assets of $1,250M minus Total current liabilities of $2,811M).

However, working capital is not a particularly useful/relevant metric for American Water Works. AWK is a regulated water utility — a capital-intensive business with highly predictable, recurring, and regulator-approved cash flows from customers. Utilities like AWK routinely operate with negative working capital because:
(1) they fund operations largely through long-term debt and continuous access to capital markets rather than short-term liquidity buffers,
(2) a large portion of current liabilities is short-term debt ($1,175M) and current portion of long-term debt ($281M) that is typically rolled over/refinanced rather than repaid from current assets, and
(3) their steady, rate-regulated revenue stream makes traditional liquidity ratios less meaningful than for a working-capital-driven business (like a manufacturer or retailer)."}

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-71#opus47-r2", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "For JnJ in FY2022, gross margin declined because Cost of Products Sold rose as a percent of sales. According to the 10-K's management commentary, the drivers were:

Headwinds (pushing COGS up / gross margin down):
• One-time COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing exit–related costs
• Currency impacts in the Pharmaceutical segment
• Commodity inflation in the MedTech and Consumer Health segments

Partial offset (helping gross margin):
• Supply-chain benefits in the Consumer Health segment

Net effect: the unfavorable items outweighed the Consumer Health supply-chain benefits, so cost of products sold rose as a % of sales and gross margin contracted in FY2022 vs. FY2021. (Note: intangible amortization in COGS actually decreased slightly, from $4.7B to $4.3B, so it was not a driver of the margin decline.)

Gross margin is a useful and relevant metric for J&J — it is a product-based healthcare company (Pharmaceuticals, MedTech, Consumer Health) whose income statement reports Cost of Products Sold against Sales, so gross margin is meaningful (unlike, e.g., a bank or pure services firm where it would not be)."}

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (PepsiCo) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of
May 27, 2022, among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 364 Day Credit
Agreement). There were no outstanding borrowings under the 2022 364 Day Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,
and expires on May 24, 2024. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the
2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or
Euros. PepsiCo may request renewal of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement for an additional 364 day period or convert any amounts outstanding into a
term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo terminated the $3,800,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of May 27, 2022, among
PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement). There were no
outstanding borrowings under the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, including a $750,000,000 swing line
subfacility for Euro-denominated borrowings permitted to be borrowed on a same day basis, subject to customary terms and conditions, and expires on
May 26, 2028. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the 2023 Five Year
Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros. PepsiCo
may, once a year, request renewal of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement for an additional one year period. Subject to certain conditions stated in the 2023

Net sales increased 18.3% to $10.2 billion compared to $8.6 billion in fiscal 2021,
primarily due to the favorable impact from the continued resilience of the beauty
category, retail price increases, the impact of new brands and product innovation,
increased social occasions, and fewer COVID-19 limitations compared to fiscal 2021.
Comparable sales increased 15.6% compared to an increase of 37.9% in fiscal 2021,

a percentage of net sales, gross profit increased to 39.6% compared to 39.0% in fiscal
2021, primarily due to leverage of fixed costs, strong growth in other revenue, and
favorable channel mix shifts, partially offset by higher inventory shrink and lower
merchandise margin.

2021. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased to 23.5% compared to
23.9% in fiscal 2021, primarily due to lower marketing expenses and leverage of
incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits
due to wage investments.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-23#opus47-r3", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "Amcor's quick ratio improved slightly from FY2022 to FY2023.

Using Quick Ratio = (Cash + Trade Receivables) / Current Liabilities (all figures $ millions):

- FY2023: (689 + 1,875) / 4,476 = 2,564 / 4,476 ≈ 0.57

Liquidity for such firms is better assessed via operating cash flow stability, credit facility availability, and interest coverage rather than the current ratio / working capital."}

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

Does Boeing have an improving gross margin profile as of FY2022? If gross margin is not a useful metric for a company like this, then state that and explain why.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-51#opus47-r3", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 1.0, "final_answer": "Yes — Boeing's gross margin profile is improving as of FY2022, though it remains very thin. Using the consolidated statements of operations:

- FY2020: Revenue $58,158M, Cost of sales $63,843M → Gross margin ≈ ‑9.8% (negative)
- FY2021: Revenue $62,286M, Cost of sales $59,269M → Gross margin ≈ 4.8%
- FY2022: Revenue $66,608M, Cost of sales $63,106M → Gross margin ≈ 5.3%

Gross margin has moved from deeply negative in 2020 (COVID + 737 MAX grounding impacts) to positive and modestly expanding in 2021 and 2022, so the trend is directionally improving. That said, gross margin is a somewhat limited metric for Boeing: it is a long-cycle aerospace/defense manufacturer that uses program- and contract-accounting (with large reach-forward losses, forward loss provisions on fixed-price defense contracts, and R&D/abnormal production costs flowing through cost of sales). This makes reported gross margin volatile and heavily influenced by charges rather than by underlying unit economics, so investors typically also look at segment operating margins and free cash flow to assess profitability trends."}

Per the FY2022 consolidated balance sheet, total current assets were $57,517M and total current liabilities were $45,101M, giving working capital of roughly +$12.4 billion.\n\nThat said, working capital is not an especially meaningful metric for PayPal. PayPal is a payments/financial-services company, not an industrial/operating-cycle business. A very large portion of its current assets and current liabilities are customer-related balances\u2014\"Funds receivable and customer accounts\" ($36.4B) on the asset side and \"Funds payable and amounts due to customers\" ($40.1B) on the liability side\u2014which are essentially pass-through balances held on behalf of customers, not resources available to fund operations or obligations arising from PayPal's own operating cycle. Because these customer balances dominate both sides of the current section and largely offset one another, standard working-capital analysis (intended to gauge short-term operating liquidity) doesn't convey the same insight it would for a manufacturer or retailer. Liquidity for PayPal is better assessed via cash and investments, regulatory capital/liquidity requirements, and its ability to meet customer redemption obligations."}

Company Overview
We were incorporated in Delaware in 1919 and reincorporated in North Carolina in 1986. We are a leading global beverage and
convenient food company with a complementary portfolio of brands, including Lays, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola,
Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream. Through our operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers and other third
parties, we make, market, distribute and sell a wide variety of beverages and convenient foods, serving customers and consumers
in more than 200 countries and territories.
Our Operations
We are organized into seven reportable segments (also referred to as divisions), as follows:
1) Frito-Lay North America (FLNA), which includes our branded convenient food businesses in the United States and
Canada;
2) Quaker Foods North America (QFNA), which includes our branded convenient food businesses, such as cereal, rice, pasta
and other branded food, in the United States and Canada;
3) PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA), which includes our beverage businesses in the United States and Canada;

Net sales increased 18.3% to $10.2 billion compared to $8.6 billion in fiscal 2021,
primarily due to the favorable impact from the continued resilience of the beauty
category, retail price increases, the impact of new brands and product innovation,
increased social occasions, and fewer COVID-19 limitations compared to fiscal 2021.

driven by a 10.8% increase in transactions and a 4.3% increase in average ticket.
Gross profit increased 20.1% to $4.0 billion compared to $3.4 billion in fiscal 2021. As
a percentage of net sales, gross profit increased to 39.6% compared to 39.0% in fiscal
2021, primarily due to leverage of fixed costs, strong growth in other revenue, and
favorable channel mix shifts, partially offset by higher inventory shrink and lower
merchandise margin.
SG&A expenses increased 16.2% to $2.4 billion compared to $2.1 billion in fiscal
2021. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased to 23.5% compared to
23.9% in fiscal 2021, primarily due to lower marketing expenses and leverage of
incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits
due to wage investments.

Using Quick Ratio = (Cash & equivalents + Trade receivables) / Total current liabilities (all figures $ millions):

- FY2022: (775 + 1,935) / 5,103 = 2,710 / 5,103 ≈ 0.53
- FY2023: (689 + 1,875) / 4,476 = 2,564 / 4,476 ≈ 0.57

As a regulated water utility, the company operates in a highly capital-intensive industry with very stable, predictable, recurring cash flows from a large customer base. Utilities like AWK routinely run negative working capital because they can reliably rely on short-term debt (commercial paper/revolving credit) and ongoing customer billings to fund near-term obligations. Liquidity for such firms is better assessed by their access to credit facilities, cash flow from operations, and regulatory rate-base recovery than by the current ratio or working capital."}

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (PepsiCo) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of
May 27, 2022, among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 364 Day Credit
Agreement). There were no outstanding borrowings under the 2022 364 Day Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,
and expires on May 24, 2024. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the
2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or
Euros. PepsiCo may request renewal of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement for an additional 364 day period or convert any amounts outstanding into a
term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

outstanding borrowings under the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, including a $750,000,000 swing line

Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros. PepsiCo
may, once a year, request renewal of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement for an additional one year period. Subject to certain conditions stated in the 2023

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

6) Africa, Middle East and South Asia (AMESA), which includes all of our beverage and convenient food businesses in

Net sales increased 18.3% to $10.2 billion compared to $8.6 billion in fiscal 2021,
primarily due to the favorable impact from the continued resilience of the beauty

increased social occasions, and fewer COVID-19 limitations compared to fiscal 2021.

favorable channel mix shifts, partially offset by higher inventory shrink and lower
merchandise margin.

2021. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased to 23.5% compared to

incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits
due to wage investments.

Utilities typically operate with negative working capital because: (1) they are capital-intensive businesses with the vast majority of assets tied up in long-lived property, plant & equipment (~$23.2B) rather than current assets; (2) they have highly predictable, recurring cash flows from regulated customers, so they don't need to hold large liquid balances; and (3) they routinely finance operations with short-term debt (which sits in current liabilities) that is regularly rolled over or refinanced with long-term debt. Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

What drove gross margin change as of FY2022 for JnJ? If gross margin is not a useful metric for a company like this, then please state that and explain why.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-71#opus47-r6", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "For JnJ in FY2022, gross margin declined because cost of products sold rose as a percentage of sales. According to JnJ's own analysis, the increase in cost of products sold (i.e., the compression in gross margin) was driven by:

1. One-time COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing exit-related costs
2. Unfavorable currency impacts in the Pharmaceutical segment
3. Commodity inflation in the MedTech and Consumer Health segments

These headwinds were partially offset by supply chain benefits in the Consumer Health segment. (Intangible asset amortization included in COGS actually decreased slightly, from $4.7B in 2021 to $4.3B in 2022, so it was not a driver of the margin decline.)

Gross margin is a useful and relevant metric for JnJ, since it is a products-based company (pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and consumer health) with a meaningful cost of products sold line — unlike a bank or pure-services firm where gross margin would not be meaningful."}

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

Does Boeing have an improving gross margin profile as of FY2022? If gross margin is not a useful metric for a company like this, then state that and explain why.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-51#opus47-r7", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 1.0, "final_answer": "Yes—on the numbers, Boeing's gross margin profile has been improving. Using the consolidated statements of operations (revenue minus total cost of sales, including Boeing Capital interest expense):

- FY2020: Revenue $58,158M, COGS $63,843M → Gross margin ≈ ‑9.8%
- FY2021: Revenue $62,286M, COGS $59,269M → Gross margin ≈ 4.8%
- FY2022: Revenue $66,608M, COGS $63,106M → Gross margin ≈ 5.3%

So gross margin has moved from deeply negative in 2020 (COVID + 737 MAX grounding aftermath) to modestly positive and rising in 2021 and 2022. The trend is improving, though margins remain very thin for an aerospace/defense manufacturer of Boeing's scale, and profitability is still being weighed down by program charges and reach-forward losses on fixed-price defense contracts. Gross margin is a reasonable, if limited, metric here—Boeing does report distinct product/service costs—so it can be used, but it should be interpreted alongside program accounting adjustments and segment results rather than in isolation."}

As a payments/financial-services company, a large portion of its current assets and liabilities are customer-related pass-through balances \u2014 \"Funds receivable and customer accounts\" ($36,357M) and \"Funds payable and amounts due to customers\" ($40,107M). These represent money PayPal is holding on behalf of users, not operating capital deployed to run the business, and they largely offset each other. Excluding these items, the picture of PayPal's operating liquidity is very different, so working capital should be interpreted with caution for this type of business."}

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (PepsiCo) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of

Agreement). There were no outstanding borrowings under the 2022 364 Day Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,
and expires on May 24, 2024. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the
2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or
Euros. PepsiCo may request renewal of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement for an additional 364 day period or convert any amounts outstanding into a
term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

subfacility for Euro-denominated borrowings permitted to be borrowed on a same day basis, subject to customary terms and conditions, and expires on

Company Overview
We were incorporated in Delaware in 1919 and reincorporated in North Carolina in 1986. We are a leading global beverage and
convenient food company with a complementary portfolio of brands, including Lays, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola,
Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream. Through our operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers and other third
parties, we make, market, distribute and sell a wide variety of beverages and convenient foods, serving customers and consumers
in more than 200 countries and territories.

Current Health Ltd.

net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

Does Boeing have an improving gross margin profile as of FY2022? If gross margin is not a useful metric for a company like this, then state that and explain why.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-51#opus47-r8", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 1.0, "final_answer": "Yes \u2014 on the reported numbers, Boeing's gross margin profile is improving as of FY2022, though it remains very thin. Using Total revenues minus Total costs and expenses (cost of products + cost of services + Boeing Capital interest expense), gross margin was roughly -9.8% in FY2020, ~4.8% in FY2021, and ~5.3% in FY2022 \u2014 a clear improvement year over year as commercial aviation recovered from the pandemic/737 MAX disruptions. That said, gross margin is a somewhat limited metric for Boeing: as a long-cycle aerospace and defense manufacturer that uses program/contract accounting, its reported cost of sales is heavily affected by items like reach-forward losses on fixed-price development programs (e.g., KC-46, VC-25B, T-7A, Commercial Crew) and 787/737 MAX abnormal production costs. These one-time charges can swing gross margin materially from period to period and obscure the underlying economics, so investors typically focus on segment operating margins, program margins, free cash flow, and backlog rather than consolidated gross margin."}

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-71#opus47-r8", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "For FY2022, Johnson & Johnson's gross margin declined because Cost of Products Sold rose as a percent of sales. Per JnJ's own disclosure, this was driven by:

1. One-time COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing exit–related costs,
2. Unfavorable currency impacts in the Pharmaceutical segment, and
3. Commodity (input) inflation in the MedTech and Consumer Health segments,

partially offset by supply chain benefits in the Consumer Health segment. (Note: intangible asset amortization included in COGS actually decreased, from $4.7B in 2021 to $4.3B in 2022, so that was a small tailwind rather than a driver of the decline.)

Gross margin is a reasonable/useful metric for JnJ since it is a products company (pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and consumer health) that reports a clear "Cost of Products Sold" line — unlike a bank or pure-services firm, where gross margin would not be meaningful."}

Company Overview
We were incorporated in Delaware in 1919 and reincorporated in North Carolina in 1986. We are a leading global beverage and
convenient food company with a complementary portfolio of brands, including Lays, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola,
Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream. Through our operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers and other third
parties, we make, market, distribute and sell a wide variety of beverages and convenient foods, serving customers and consumers
in more than 200 countries and territories.
Our Operations
We are organized into seven reportable segments (also referred to as divisions), as follows:
1) Frito-Lay North America (FLNA), which includes our branded convenient food businesses in the United States and
Canada;
2) Quaker Foods North America (QFNA), which includes our branded convenient food businesses, such as cereal, rice, pasta
and other branded food, in the United States and Canada;
3) PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA), which includes our beverage businesses in the United States and Canada;
4) Latin America (LatAm), which includes all of our beverage and convenient food businesses in Latin America;
5) Europe, which includes all of our beverage and convenient food businesses in Europe;

6) Africa, Middle East and South Asia (AMESA), which includes all of our beverage and convenient food businesses in
Africa, the Middle East and South Asia; and
7) Asia Pacific, Australia and New Zealand and China Region (APAC), which includes all of our beverage and convenient
food businesses in Asia Pacific, Australia and New Zealand, and China region.

- Quick ratio ≈ 27,111 / 50,171 ≈ 0.54

A quick ratio below 1.0 means Verizon's most liquid assets cover only about 54% of its short-term obligations, so on a strict quick-ratio basis liquidity looks weak. That said, for a large telecom like Verizon the quick ratio is of limited relevance — it generates very stable, recurring subscription cash flows, has strong ongoing operating cash flow (over $37B in 2022) and ready access to commercial paper and revolving credit facilities, so it does not need to hold quick assets sufficient to cover current liabilities. Liquidity for such a company is better assessed via operating cash flow coverage and available credit capacity than via the quick ratio."}

Using the balance sheet ($ in millions, as of June 30):

Quick ratio = (Cash + Trade Receivables) / Current Liabilities

- FY2023: (689 + 1,875) / 4,476 = 2,564 / 4,476 ≈ 0.57
- FY2022: (775 + 1,935) / 5,103 = 2,710 / 5,103 ≈ 0.53

So the quick ratio rose from ~0.53 in FY2022 to ~0.57 in FY2023 — a slight improvement, driven mainly by a larger drop in current liabilities (chiefly trade payables) than in liquid current assets. Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

- FY2022: Revenue $66,608M; Total costs $63,106M → Gross margin ≈ 5.3%

So gross margin has expanded from deeply negative in 2020 to ~4.8% in 2021 to ~5.3% in 2022 — an improving trend, though the level remains very low and the pace of improvement slowed meaningfully between 2021 and 2022 (only ~40 bps). Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (PepsiCo) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of
May 27, 2022, among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 364 Day Credit
Agreement). There were no outstanding borrowings under the 2022 364 Day Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,
and expires on May 24, 2024. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the
2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or
Euros. PepsiCo may request renewal of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement for an additional 364 day period or convert any amounts outstanding into a
term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo terminated the $3,800,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of May 27, 2022, among
PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement). There were no
outstanding borrowings under the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, including a $750,000,000 swing line
subfacility for Euro-denominated borrowings permitted to be borrowed on a same day basis, subject to customary terms and conditions, and expires on
May 26, 2028. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the 2023 Five Year
Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros. PepsiCo
may, once a year, request renewal of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement for an additional one year period. Subject to certain conditions stated in the 2023
Five Year Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under the 2023 Five Year Credit
Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement may be used
for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement contains customary representations and warranties

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-23#opus47-r10", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "AMCOR's quick ratio improved slightly between FY2022 and FY2023.

Using Quick Ratio = (Current Assets − Inventories − Prepaid Expenses − Assets Held for Sale) / Current Liabilities (equivalent here to (Cash + Trade Receivables) / Current Liabilities):

- FY2022: (775 + 1,935) / 5,103 ≈ 0.53
- FY2023: (689 + 1,875) / 4,476 ≈ 0.57

So the quick ratio rose from ~0.53 to ~0.57, a modest improvement of roughly 0.04 (about 8%), driven primarily by a larger decline in current liabilities (mainly trade payables and short-term debt) than in liquid current assets. Note that in both years the ratio is well below 1.0, indicating Amcor's liquid assets alone do not cover its short-term liabilities — typical for a large, working-capital-intensive packaging manufacturer that relies on inventory turnover and stable operating cash flow rather than on holding cash/receivables."}

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

Net sales increased 18.3% to $10.2 billion compared to $8.6 billion in fiscal 2021,
primarily due to the favorable impact from the continued resilience of the beauty
category, retail price increases, the impact of new brands and product innovation,
increased social occasions, and fewer COVID-19 limitations compared to fiscal 2021.
Comparable sales increased 15.6% compared to an increase of 37.9% in fiscal 2021,
driven by a 10.8% increase in transactions and a 4.3% increase in average ticket.

a percentage of net sales, gross profit increased to 39.6% compared to 39.0% in fiscal
2021, primarily due to leverage of fixed costs, strong growth in other revenue, and
favorable channel mix shifts, partially offset by higher inventory shrink and lower
merchandise margin.
SG&A expenses increased 16.2% to $2.4 billion compared to $2.1 billion in fiscal
2021. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased to 23.5% compared to
23.9% in fiscal 2021, primarily due to lower marketing expenses and leverage of
incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits
due to wage investments.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-23#opus47-r11", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "Amcor's quick ratio improved slightly between FY2022 and FY2023.

Using the formula Quick Ratio = (Cash & Cash Equivalents + Trade Receivables) / Total Current Liabilities:

- FY2022: ($775M + $1,935M) / $5,103M ≈ 0.53
- FY2023: ($689M + $1,875M) / $4,476M ≈ 0.57

So the quick ratio improved by roughly 0.04 (from ~0.53 to ~0.57), driven mainly by a larger decline in current liabilities (notably trade payables) than in liquid current assets. Note, however, that the ratio remains below 1.0, meaning Amcor's most-liquid assets alone do not cover its current liabilities — this is typical for a large, working-capital-intensive packaging manufacturer that relies on inventory turnover and steady operating cash flow, so analysts generally focus more on leverage, free cash flow, and interest coverage than on the quick ratio for a company like Amcor."}

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

For the Full Year of Fiscal 2022
Net sales increased 18.3% to $10.2 billion compared to $8.6 billion in fiscal 2021,
primarily due to the favorable impact from the continued resilience of the beauty
category, retail price increases, the impact of new brands and product innovation,
increased social occasions, and fewer COVID-19 limitations compared to fiscal 2021.
Comparable sales increased 15.6% compared to an increase of 37.9% in fiscal 2021,
driven by a 10.8% increase in transactions and a 4.3% increase in average ticket.
Gross profit increased 20.1% to $4.0 billion compared to $3.4 billion in fiscal 2021. As
a percentage of net sales, gross profit increased to 39.6% compared to 39.0% in fiscal
2021, primarily due to leverage of fixed costs, strong growth in other revenue, and
favorable channel mix shifts, partially offset by higher inventory shrink and lower
merchandise margin.
SG&A expenses increased 16.2% to $2.4 billion compared to $2.1 billion in fiscal
2021. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased to 23.5% compared to
23.9% in fiscal 2021, primarily due to lower marketing expenses and leverage of
incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits
due to wage investments.

Does Verizon have a reasonably healthy liquidity profile based on its quick ratio for FY 2022? If the quick ratio is not relevant to measure liquidity, please state that and explain why.

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-115#opus47-r11", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 1.0, "final_answer": "No. Verizon's FY2022 quick ratio is approximately 0.54, which is well below 1.0 and therefore does not indicate a "healthy" liquidity profile on that metric alone.

Calculation (from the FY2022 balance sheet, $ in millions):
- Cash & cash equivalents: $2,605
- Accounts receivable, net: $24,506
- (Inventories $2,388 and prepaid expenses $8,358 are excluded from the quick ratio)
- Quick assets = 2,605 + 24,506 = $27,111
- Total current liabilities = $50,171
- Quick ratio = 27,111 / 50,171 ≈ 0.54

Caveat: For a large, investment-grade telecom like Verizon, the quick ratio is of limited usefulness as a liquidity measure. Verizon generates very stable, recurring subscription cash flows and has ready access to capital markets and committed credit facilities, so it deliberately runs with current liabilities greater than current assets (a common pattern among capital-intensive utilities/telecoms). Liquidity is better assessed via operating cash flow, free cash flow, and available credit lines rather than the quick ratio."}

Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

3. Commodity/input-cost inflation in the MedTech and Consumer Health segments,

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-99#opus47-r12", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "Yes \u2014 technically PayPal had positive working capital in FY2022: Total current assets of $57,517M minus Total current liabilities of $45,101M = approximately +$12,416M.\n\nHowever, working capital is not a particularly meaningful/useful metric for PayPal. As a payments platform, a large share of its current assets and current liabilities represents customer custodial balances \u2014 \"Funds receivable and customer accounts\" ($36,357M in 2022) is offset by a nearly identical \"Funds payable and amounts due to customers\" on the liability side. These are pass-through balances held on behalf of customers, not resources available to fund PayPal's own operations, so the traditional working-capital calculation does not reflect the company's true short-term liquidity position. Liquidity for a financial-services/payments company like PayPal is better assessed via metrics such as available cash and investments, regulatory capital, and liquidity coverage rather than working capital."}

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (PepsiCo) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of
May 27, 2022, among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 364 Day Credit
Agreement). There were no outstanding borrowings under the 2022 364 Day Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, subject to customary terms and conditions,
and expires on May 24, 2024. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the
2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or
Euros. PepsiCo may request renewal of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement for an additional 364 day period or convert any amounts outstanding into a
term loan for a period of up to one year, which term loan would mature no later than the anniversary of the then effective termination date. Subject to
certain conditions stated in the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under
the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement may be used for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 364 Day Credit Agreement contains customary
representations and warranties and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 364 Day Credit
Agreement and their affiliates have engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo
and its affiliates.

Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo terminated the $3,800,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of May 27, 2022, among
PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement). There were no
outstanding borrowings under the 2022 Five Year Credit Agreement at the time of its termination.

On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered into a new $4,200,000,000 five year unsecured revolving credit agreement (the 2023 Five Year Credit
Agreement) among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement
enables PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries to borrow up to $4,200,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, including a $750,000,000 swing line
subfacility for Euro-denominated borrowings permitted to be borrowed on a same day basis, subject to customary terms and conditions, and expires on
May 26, 2028. PepsiCo may also, upon the agreement of either the then existing lenders or of additional banks not currently party to the 2023 Five Year
Credit Agreement, increase the commitments under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement to up to $4,950,000,000 in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros. PepsiCo
may, once a year, request renewal of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement for an additional one year period. Subject to certain conditions stated in the 2023
Five Year Credit Agreement, PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries may borrow, prepay and reborrow amounts under the 2023 Five Year Credit
Agreement at any time during the term of the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement. Funds borrowed under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement may be used
for general corporate purposes of PepsiCo and its subsidiaries. The 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement contains customary representations and warranties
and events of default. In the ordinary course of their respective businesses, the lenders under the 2023 Five Year Credit Agreement and their affiliates have
engaged, and may in the future engage, in commercial banking and/or investment banking transactions with PepsiCo and its affiliates.---

category, retail price increases, the impact of new brands and product innovation,

incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-5#opus47-r13", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 1.0, "final_answer": "3M's Q2 FY2023 (June 30, 2023) quick ratio is approximately 0.85, which suggests a somewhat weak liquidity profile on that specific metric.

Calculation: Quick Ratio = (Cash & equivalents + Marketable securities + Accounts receivable) / Total current liabilities
= ($4,258M + $56M + $4,947M) / $10,936M
= $9,261M / $10,936M ≈ 0.85

A quick ratio below 1.0 indicates that 3M's most liquid assets (excluding inventory and prepaids) would not fully cover its current liabilities. So strictly on the quick ratio, 3M's liquidity looks somewhat stretched rather than robustly healthy. That said, for a large, cash-generative industrial like 3M with strong operating cash flow and ample access to capital markets, a quick ratio slightly below 1 is not necessarily alarming — but by the quick ratio measure alone, it is not "reasonably healthy.""}

{"benchmark": "financebench", "task_id": "fb-train-37#opus47-r13", "model": "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7", "split": "train", "reward": 0.0, "final_answer": "No. Based on FY2022 data, American Water Works had NEGATIVE working capital of approximately -$1,561 million (Total current assets of $1,250M minus Total current liabilities of $2,811M).

That said, working capital is not a particularly useful or relevant liquidity metric for American Water Works. As a regulated water utility, the company:
• Generates highly predictable, recurring cash flows from a large, rate-regulated customer base, so it does not need a current-asset cushion to meet near-term obligations.
• Funds operations and its heavy capital-expenditure program largely through continuous access to short-term debt / commercial paper (about $1,175M outstanding in FY2022) and committed revolving credit facilities, which shows up as current liabilities but is routinely rolled/refinanced.
• Deploys most of its capital into long-lived property, plant and equipment (~$23.2B) rather than current assets like inventory or receivables.

For these reasons, regulated utilities such as AWK typically run with structurally negative working capital, and liquidity is better assessed via operating cash flow, credit-facility availability, and access to debt markets rather than the current ratio or working capital."}

Acquisitions
 
Current Health Ltd.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (Current Health), a care-at-home technology platform, on November 2, 2021, for 
net cash consideration of $389 million. The acquired assets included $351 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Health reporting unit and was 
deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition is aligned with our focus in virtual care to enable people in their homes to connect seamlessly with their 
health care providers and is included in our Domestic reportable segment and Services revenue category. The acquisition was accounted for using the 
acquisition method of accounting for business combinations and was not material to the results of operations.
 
Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (Yardbird), a direct-to-consumer outdoor furniture company, 
on November 4, 2021, for net cash consideration of $79 million. The acquired assets included $47 million of goodwill that was assigned to our Best Buy Domestic 
reporting unit and was deductible for income tax purposes. The acquisition expands our assortment in categories like outdoor living, as more and more 
consumers look to make over or upgrade their outdoor living spaces. The acquisition was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting for business 
combinations and was not material to the results of our operations.

For the Full Year of Fiscal 2022
Net sales increased 18.3% to $10.2 billion compared to $8.6 billion in fiscal 2021,
primarily due to the favorable impact from the continued resilience of the beauty
category, retail price increases, the impact of new brands and product innovation,
increased social occasions, and fewer COVID-19 limitations compared to fiscal 2021.

Gross profit increased 20.1% to $4.0 billion compared to $3.4 billion in fiscal 2021. As
a percentage of net sales, gross profit increased to 39.6% compared to 39.0% in fiscal
2021, primarily due to leverage of fixed costs, strong growth in other revenue, and
favorable channel mix shifts, partially offset by higher inventory shrink and lower
merchandise margin.
SG&A expenses increased 16.2% to $2.4 billion compared to $2.1 billion in fiscal
2021. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased to 23.5% compared to
23.9% in fiscal 2021, primarily due to lower marketing expenses and leverage of
incentive compensation due to higher sales, partially offset by deleverage of corporate
overhead due to strategic investments and deleverage of store payroll and benefits
due to wage investments.
